original_card.question: Can one small, precisely scoped interface lemma be formalized with its actual hypotheses?
methods: Formalize a missing boundary lemma identified by the selected review.
Audit a formal theorem-to-certificate binding independently.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State the exact formalized proposition and remaining assumptions; avoid duplicate arithmetic formalizations already present.

first_step.inspect: Read the exact hypotheses in the hyperplane-end proof and distinguish Lean theorems from finite supplier assumptions.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: State one missing boundary lemma in full before starting a proof-assistant build.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A missing interface proof can reduce the conditional gap even if it does not change kappa.
allowed_variations: Narrow to one formal lemma or one theorem-to-certificate binding.
scope_change_triggers: Formalizing already-covered arithmetic and claiming the full multiplication theorem.

actual_scope: Independent E8 frame-stabilizer and PR1212 Section 8/10 theorem-to-floor audit, including a new type-(4,4) P104 pivot with an independently built and stdlib-RUP-verified zero-exclusion certificate.
scope_change_reason: Session16 audited PR1560 Theorem 1 and its P107-P105 binding while explicitly leaving PR1212 Sections 8 and 10. The alternate pivot arose while checking Section 10 and gives a direct application of PR1212 original Lemmas 5-7 to a type-(4,4) unit already settled by PR1389 through a new gluing lemma.
bottleneck_link: Source-bound proof of the exact eight-costly-term E-graph floor narrows decoder mechanisms; this audit improves reviewability of a finite interface without changing the selected supplier or kappa.
stop_rule: Stop after an independent 120-line, 2025-frame and 1260-second-frame orbit census, signed Gram/cost transport, 24 alternate type-(4,4) pivot census, complete class/witness checks, a new reduced zero-pattern CNF and RUP proof, PR1212 Section 8 written audit, source pins, failure controls and registered replay. Do not redo PR1389 or search nine-term decoders.
evidence: RESULT.json and stdlib verify.py: 2025 Weyl-transitive frames, 204 FRAME0 stabilizer generators, one 112-line orbit and 28/336/896 second-frame orbits; on PR1212's own type-(4,4) unit (deleted frame {2,3,16,17,46,47,52,53} in PR1212 numbering), 25 of 801 live pivots have no incomplete class: PR1212's pivot covers 12 blocks and 24 others cover all 14. At the alternate pivot {12,13,22,23,30,31,36,37}: 288 class witnesses, 1952 ordered sign-rule gluing checks, and an independently encoded two+diagonal zero-pattern CNF (1152 variables, 16865 clauses including some-zero) refuted by a 2501-addition proof replayed by the stdlib RUP checker. With PR1212 Lemmas 5-7 this gives a second route to the type-(4,4) rank-eight rigidity already proved by PR1389.
author: Josie Elliston
ai_assistance: Substantial AI assistance: prepared by OpenAI Codex (offline session 17b: audit, exact verifier, proof generation, controls and writing); reviewed, corrected and published by Claude (Anthropic, session 19). No independent human review.

open_questions.question: Can the alternate complete-pivot certificate simplify a future formalization of type-(4,4) rigidity?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It uses PR1212 original complete-class and gluing lemmas without PR1389's additional gluing lemma 6′.
open_questions.first_step: Formalize the new finite zero-pattern CNF implication and cite the shipped 2501-addition RUP proof, then bind the four finite hypotheses to Lemmas 5-7.
open_questions.blocked_by: The RUP proof and written Lemmas 5-7 are checked by programs and review, not a proof assistant.

open_questions.question: Does the alternate pivot's two-term/diagonal refutation have a short human-readable core?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A readable reason would remove the solver certificate from the type-(4,4) proof; at PR1212's own pivot these two families do not exclude zeros.
open_questions.first_step: Compute a deletion-minimal unsatisfiable core of the shipped CNF and compare it with PR1212's recorded 380-group P112 core.
open_questions.blocked_by: No evidence yet that such a core is small.
